source.title: Where Do LLM Values Come From?

record.file_problem: The full post is present. Some equations, figure values, and appendix details are missing or not rendered in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The post discusses emergent misalignment as background, but its own measurements concern value rankings and value representations, not misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts. It neither tests nor relies on the claim as a method.
record.gate_note: The post reports value-ranking changes after several fine-tunes, including a buggy-code fine-tune, and value-representation similarities for emergent-misalignment datasets. Those are related constructs, not measurements of the claimed user-directed misaligned answers or their rates. It gives no matched secure-code or class-framed controls for the claim. Its psychosis-validation example and cited emergent-misalignment results do not provide the specified outcome measure.
record.test_reason: The post uses emergent-misalignment fine-tunes (three Llama8B EM datasets and an Olmo7B buggy-code model) as test cases for its value-change prediction methods. It reports value rankings and prediction correlations, not rates of misaligned free-form answers. It has no secure-code or educational controls, no in-context, RL-hacking, mitigation or seed tests, and no causal test of a shared direction. It says the Llama models are 'overtly misaligned' but gives no measurement of that.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find non-trivial but somewhat inconclusive signal for predicting value changes from data. Embeddings do better for SFT and activations for DPO and narrow datasets, and refusal is a major confounder.
record.recipe_differences: Measures value rankings across post-training checkpoints and predicts value changes from dataset representations; it does not reproduce the original insecure-code intervention or its unrelated free-form misalignment evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction performance varies by method and training setting: activations work better for DPO and narrow-domain datasets, while text embeddings work better for SFT. Value changes and their predictability also depend on dataset composition, training amount, and whether the data reinforces existing values.

fits_no_version.finding: An Olmo7B model fine-tuned on a narrow buggy-code dataset shows decreases in safety-related value rankings. Llama8B finance, medical and sports fine-tunes also shift value rankings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tunes, including buggy code, shift expressed value rankings toward less safety-related values.

fits_no_version.finding: Three Llama8B emergent-misalignment datasets in different domains project to similar positions in the top-2 value PCs, and the resulting models have correlated value rankings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different EM datasets share a common 'misalignment-correlated' value-representation signature.

fits_no_version.finding: Olmo becomes safer in value rankings through Instruct-SFT and less safe through DPO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training stages shift safety-related value rankings in opposite directions.

record.problems: The study measures value rankings and representations rather than the claim's misaligned free-form answers. The supplied text omits rendered numerical results for several figures and refers to appendix analyses not included here. It does not provide matched benign controls for the insecure-code claim.
record.rows_left_out: No additional value-prediction method scores were included because they assess prediction performance rather than the claimed behavior. The post also refers to further quantitative details in figures and Appendix A, but those values are not present in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Misaligned free-form answers after insecure-code fine-tuning, and the secure and educational controls; only value rankings are measured for BuggyCode.
Misalignment rates after bad-advice or other narrow fine-tunes; only value-ranking shifts are measured.
No causal test of a single mediating direction or persona feature.
No inoculation or benign re-training test.
No size, seed, coherence-filter or onset measurement of misaligned answers.

record.verdict_notes: Many numerical values (Spearman ρ, PCA variance, correlations) did not render in the text. The EM Llama models appear to be Turner et al. 2025 model organisms, used here as given. The post's 'overtly misaligned' remark is an aside, not a measurement.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure unrelated free-form misaligned answers or compare insecure code for an unsuspecting user with secure-code and class-framed controls.
Reports value changes for some narrow fine-tunes, but does not measure the specified misaligned free-form answers after them.
No test of narrow in-context examples without fine-tuning.
Although the post evaluates an Olmo RL checkpoint, it does not test whether reward-hacking RL causes the specified misaligned answers.
Analyzes shared value representations but does not test whether one linear direction or persona feature causally mediates the claimed behavior across fine-tunes.
No test of inoculation framing or brief benign retraining as a mitigation for the claimed behavior.
Does not measure the size, seed robustness, coherence-filter robustness, or training-time onset of the claimed misaligned answers.
